name: operators — equals on a contactInfo (object-shaped) answer -> no-match (TS<->PY drift-guard)
description: FROZEN drift-guard (FU-1). The host question 'gate' runs `equals` against the answer of the contactInfo question 'contact', whose answer is an OBJECT ({firstName, email}). Per the operator `$comment` in survey-schema.json, the equality-family operators (equals/notEquals/isOneOf) treat an object-shaped answer as NOT a valid comparison target -> equals deterministically returns FALSE in BOTH languages (Python no longer deep-compares dicts; TS deepEqual already returns false for non-array objects). So the jumpTo does NOT fire and we advance linearly to 'next'. This pins the validator-reachable consequence of the no-match rule (equals on contactInfo is the only equality-family/object-answer pairing validateSurvey permits — isOneOf is not a contactInfo operator and matrix permits only isSubmitted/isSkipped). Note: a schema-valid `value` cannot itself be an object (conditionLeaf.value forbids it), so the historical deep-compare divergence was never reachable in a valid survey; this fixture locks in the documented semantics regardless.

name: operators — notEquals on a contactInfo (object-shaped) answer -> vacuously true, fires (TS<->PY drift-guard)
description: FROZEN drift-guard (FU-1), complement of the equals case. `notEquals` against the object-shaped 'contact' answer is VACUOUSLY TRUE (an object is not a valid equality-family target), so the rule fires and jumpTo 'flagged' is taken — identically in TS and Python. Pins the notEquals->true branch of the no-match rule.
